node.title: Re: Why is this exit code -1?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Have a look at the [doc://system|documentation] (Update: you'll also find some example code there how to inspect [doc://system] for errors):

Return value of -1 indicates a failure to start the program or an error of the [man://wait;2|wait(2)] system call (inspect [doc://$!] for the reason).

And turn on [doc://warnings]:

$ perl -wMstrict -le 'print system("exit 3");print "<$!>"' Can't exec "exit": No such file or directory at -e line 1. -1

exit is a shell [https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Bourne-Shell-Builtins.html#index-exit|builtin], not an actual system command.

$ which exit $ perl -wMstrict -le 'print system(q{/bin/bash -c "exit 3"}); print "<$!>\n",$?>>8' 768 <> 3

And the AM [id://1225367|post] explains why the shell doesn't get called in my first example above:

$ perl -wMstrict -le 'system("pstree -A $$ ")==0 or die;' perl---pstree $ perl -wMstrict -le 'system("pstree -A $$;")==0 or die;' perl---sh---pstree

By the way, I can recommend [mod://IPC::System::Simple] because of its better error handling, and I would also recommend avoiding the shell, if possible - I wrote about the issues with it [id://1180578|here], and fellow monk [afoken] wrote about [id://1205217].
